title: Lecturer on Oral Health Policy and Epidemiology, Part-time
bio: Originally from Khartoum, Sudan, Omer Elrayah has embarked on a remarkable journey characterized by a deep commitment to education and a fervent desire for positive change. This is exemplified through his Bachelor's degree in Biochemistry from Saint Anselm College (2017) and a master’s degree in Oral Health Sciences from Boston University School of Medicine (2018). His academic prowess is highlighted further through Doctor of Dental Medicine degree from Tufts University School of Dental Medicine (Class of 2022). As a testament to his dedication to improving dental care he decided to pursue research on the “Effects of oral health in relation to fluoridation and socioeconomic status in developed and developing countries”. This stands as a testament to his dedication to improving global dental care. https://hdl.handle.net/2144/33014 Furthermore, Omer has actively engaged in research at the renowned Forsyth Institute, further honing his skills and knowledge in the field of dentistry. However, Omer’s journey is not solely defined by academic excellence, as his experiences during visits to Sudan, fueled his determination to challenge the prevailing perception of dentistry. He envisions a world where dental care is an essential component of life rather than a luxury. With his extensive educational background, research contributions, and unwavering commitment to change, Omer aspires to make dentistry accessible and valued globally, particularly in underserved communities, leaving an indelible mark on the field of oral health.
